name: AshesiGhana
title: Recovering Gold from E-Waste / SynMine
relevance: technique to borrow
why: the only entry here that reports building the whole physical chain — grinder and reactor included — around a biological process, with a GolS-based biosensor reporting gold concentration in solution as an in-line efficiency metric, and a chain-level model. They also claim selectivity for Au(I) while copper, nickel, zinc and tin stay in solution, and that engagement with Agbogbloshie workers, miners and Ghana's EPA shaped design decisions. Numbers for recovery per pass are absent.

name: BGCFullerton
title: MycoVela: Protecting Mycorrhizal Fungi for Future Space Agriculture
relevance: same space
why: `same space` — a cell-free antioxidant carrier that protects Rhizophagus irregularis spores and hyphae from oxidative stress in lunar regolith simulant, using pyomelanin made by heterologous HPPD expression in E. coli and a catalase designed for activity in regolith. They state the Earth application plainly: better AMF symbiosis raises crop yield. Honest about status — the experiments are "proposed", with named controls (pyomelanin carrier vs ascorbic acid vs carrier-only vs stress-only) and named readouts (spore viability, hyphal growth, oxidative-stress response). A designed control set with no data yet is still a usable template.

name: BNUZH-China
title: PineProtector
relevance: direct competitor; the kill switch is the main thing to take home.
why: *B. subtilis* colonising pine trunks, expressing a protease under a phenolic-acid-induced system plus a Bt toxin — and a KillerRed-based suicide switch where leaving the tree means sunlight exposure, ROS production and death. That is a light-triggered biocontainment design, which is both ReLeaf's weak spot (kill switches) and ReLeaf's own actuator (light) used in the opposite direction.

name: CAU-China
title: Fungal Sentinel
relevance: technique to borrow on low-cost optical measurement; the nanomolar claim from a phone camera is the one to probe.
why: OptiX, a phone-based fluorimeter costing about $15 in materials, which resolves the reporter spectrum from RAW camera images down to nanomolar levels. Spectral unmixing from a phone RAW file is a cheaper and more interesting measurement route than a dedicated photodiode chain. The living half — a rewired yeast mating pathway with an olfactory receptor and a Gpa1–Gαolf chimera — is a clean example of repurposing native signalling.

name: Gikal
title: ZipTide: designing short peptides against zonulin-driven loss of the intestinal barrier
relevance: ** Benchmark — this is the template for how BoPep4 should have been selected and pre-registered.
why: The most disciplined peptide-design funnel in the slice, and the most honest: 25.6 billion 8-mers collapsed onto 2,220,075 compositions without discarding any, ranked by physicochemical distance to larazotide, 1,500 screened for toxicity/allergenicity/haemolysis, 20 docked, 3 synthesised. The success criterion was written before any data existed, the gliadin assay worked (zonulin up 4.8-fold, reversed by larazotide), and they report that neither tested candidate cleared the bar and the third arrived as an empty vial.

name: HAS
title: AstroFlora: Solutions for Plant Growth in Microgravity
relevance: same space
why: `same space` — an engineered E. coli plant probiotic that reduces excessive ABA and IAA accumulation in roots under microgravity stress, plus Floraspin, their own hardware for simulating microgravity plant growth, verified as promoting Arabidopsis germination. Lowering a stress hormone in the root with a bacterium is structurally the same intervention as our ACC deaminase lowering ethylene; they have a plant readout, which is a weakness of ours. How a bacterium reduces plant hormone levels is not explained in the abstract.

name: HKU-HongKong
title: Omni-Patch
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — the design-to-release-kinetics chain is the same chain we need from BoPep4 through the membrane.
why: A de novo pipeline with named tools — RFdiffusion, LigandMPNN, molecular dynamics — aimed at a specific interface (MD-2/LPS in the TLR4 complex), producing lead αTi-14 that reduced cell-associated fluorescent LPS in macrophage-like cells. They state plainly that functional confirmation is still ongoing, and their mathematical model links molecular design to alginate release kinetics and downstream response.

name: Ionis-Paris
title: NEWT
relevance: direct competitor on conditional protectant release into a recirculating system.
why: Closed-loop hydroponics is the deployment setting, which is ReLeaf's setting. They engineer *Pseudomonas putida* to release lytic enzymes only on recognition of *Pythium* cell-wall biomarkers, via a two-component system with a biomarker-binding module — a conditional release design driven by a pathogen signal rather than an operator's light. They state the open question honestly: whether the enzyme expresses and stays bioactive.

name: KAIST Korea
title: RATAtouille: Multi-Layer Genetic Circuits for Dynamic Metabolic Control
relevance: benchmark
why: the framing is the sharpest in the slice — performance is decided by *when* genes switch on, not which are present — and they build input modules reading precursor level, population density and an external signal into one shared output format, then use hierarchical logic so the delay through each layer splits the pathway in time. Their test case is lutein, where a promiscuous cyclase feeds both product and byproduct and cannot be deleted, so timing is the only lever. No titres, fold changes or delay measurements appear in the abstract.

name: KAUST-KSA
title: SHIHAB
relevance: same space
why: `same space` — B. subtilis is one of three chassis (with S. cerevisiae and P. pastoris), engineered for radiation and stress resilience, and the whole thing is integrated into a custom-designed bioreactor built for operation under space conditions for autonomous on-demand protein production. On-demand production in a purpose-built vessel is our exact claim; theirs is for astronauts rather than plants. The abstract names no therapeutic, no titre, and no bioreactor specification, so the vessel may be a design rather than a build.

name: Korea-HS
title: Melano Shield
relevance: none but instructive
why: not our field at all, and the best measurement writing in the slice. They report 419 mg/L dried pigment, matching a commercial Sepia melanin standard to within 0.5% in log-linear absorbance slope, an empty-vector control giving none, mass loss of 3.06 ± 0.73% against 9.36 ± 1.82% untreated oak and 3.67 ± 0.73% for a commercial product — then state plainly that at three specimens per condition they match that product and do not beat it, and that this is to their knowledge the first fire test of a bacterially produced melanin coating. A high-school team is modelling the reporting standard we want for our own chlorophyll and DNPH numbers.

name: Latvia-Riga
title: TRACE
relevance: technique to borrow on display and on non-genetic containment.
why: *B. subtilis* spore display, fusing passenger proteins to native CotB, CotC and CotG coat proteins with sfGFP as a size placeholder for nanobodies — and an Fe-EDTA-ethanol protocol that renders the spores non-viable before release. Surface display plus a chemical inactivation step is a biocontainment route GEMS has not considered, and the shelf-stable-bioreagent framing is a different product shape.

name: LethbridgeHS
title: Oat Shield: Sustainable cellulose bandages with integrated antimicrobial peptides
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — their subtilin expression and purification route is a direct comparator for our peptide work, and the ag-waste framing is a model for how to connect to Taiwanese agriculture.
why: The only team in the slice working on our organism's product: subtilin, the antimicrobial peptide from *Bacillus subtilis*, expressed heterologously in *E. coli* under an IPTG-inducible promoter with a hexahistidine tag. The material half — cellulose extracted from oat husk agricultural waste — is the one genuine agriculture/sustainable-materials crossover in the health villages.

name: McMaster-Canada
title: Chariot: A Platform Technology for OMV-based Therapeutics
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — this is the closest thing in the slice to our problem of getting a protein out of the cell and across a membrane, with hardware attached.
why: They attack the real bottleneck in vesicle production — yield and variability — with vesicle nucleating peptide tags to load cargo into outer membrane vesicles, and they built the kit around it: a custom bioreactor and a microfluidic OMV isolation device, plus two in silico tools for de novo cargo generation and VNp sequence optimisation.

name: NCKU-Tainan
title: Capture: A Dual-Action Biosensor and Inhibitor for Pseudomonas aeruginosa
relevance: ** Technique to borrow (fluorescent readout calibration) and new direction (retron-generated ssDNA as a tunable binder source); plus a Taiwan network contact.
why: An AHL biosensor giving a visible fluorescent readout for low-cost screening, paired with a retron system producing ssDNA aptamers that bind AHL — using retrons to make aptamers in vivo is unusual in this slice. Also the other Taiwanese team in the health villages, so the booth doubles as a domestic contact. The abstract's inhibition claims (swarming, pyocyanin, biofilm) are stated without numbers.

name: NU Boston
title: Soil Shield
relevance: technique to borrow on both biocontainment measurement and field-condition testing.
why: Three things GEMS needs, in one project: a salicylate-dependent kill switch characterised by flow cytometry rather than plate counts, biodegradable alginate beads as the soil delivery vehicle, and a purpose-built soil chamber to test in dry post-wildfire conditions. Field validation on real substrate plus a quantified kill switch is the combination ReLeaf lacks.

name: SZ-SHD
title: S.A.F.E. Crops
relevance: direct competitor. The abstract is all future tense, so expect little data; the chassis and delivery-route choices are the prize.
why: *B. subtilis* 168Δ4 as a frost-resilient endophyte with a low-temperature-responsive circuit that autonomously controls synthesis and release of antifreeze proteins or protective sugars. Same architecture as ReLeaf — environmental input, conditional protectant production, release to the plant — with temperature as the input instead of light, and the Δ4 protease-deficient strain is a chassis choice GEMS should have an opinion on.

name: UCSC
title: AMPiary
relevance: technique to borrow
why: a modular antimicrobial-peptide manufacturing pipeline — a standardised AMP expression plasmid plus AMPexchange, which swaps the AMP gene without full reassembly — in E. coli hosts carrying a dual-mechanism biosafety system, with a ML genetic algorithm (reVAMP) that improves on assay data. They designed, synthesised, purified and validated one novel peptide, apiarin. This is the BoPep4 problem solved as a platform: peptide production plus containment plus a design loop closed with real assay data.

name: UPF-Barcelona
title: Vinesys
relevance: direct competitor, and an alternative to light as the conditional trigger. ReLeaf should be able to say why light beats an osmotic/intein AND-gate.
why: *B. subtilis* colonising vine roots, overexpressing γ-PGA for water retention *and* ACC deaminase — plus the most interesting control logic in the slice: a two-factor gate combining an osmotic stress promoter with a salt-dependent intein that only splices when intracellular K⁺ rises, so the protein is functional only when both agree. They also report the gate does not work yet: candidate intein HutMCM2 activates at 1.5 M salt while the chassis only reaches 600–725 mM, and lowering it was attempted in silico.

name: YHA-HWFLA
title: Fel d1 Eraser
relevance: same space
why: `same space` by mechanism — precise optogenetic regulation of enzyme activity, shipped as a product pair: a light-protective spray plus a portable blue-light activator. That is our light panel reduced to a consumer handheld, and they also claim to have established standardised parts for heterologous protease expression. Light-controlled enzyme activity in a formulation the user triggers is a delivery idea we have not considered for the membrane release step. No degradation percentages, intensities or exposure times appear.

name: BJWZ-China
title: Tree Guard
relevance: direct competitor on chassis and on secretion; technique to borrow on fusion-protein secretion.
why: Engineered *B. subtilis* that continuously secretes a LysM₃-chitinase fusion inside a living peach tree — continuous secretion of a multi-domain protein from this chassis, in planta, which is exactly the gap in ReLeaf. They also claim laboratory confirmation of hyphal inhibition, so there should be a real assay behind it.

name: Concordia-Montreal
title: BiblioTK: Engineering a Gram-Positive Toolkit System
relevance: same space
why: `same space` by parts rather than application — they extend SubtiToolKit, the B. subtilis Golden Gate standard, with Part E (modular, independently exchangeable origins of replication inside STK's grammar) and pGRAMLIN, a split-marker shuttle vector that couples antibiotic selection to correct recircularisation to raise transformation efficiency in Gram-positive hosts. Transformation efficiency and vector choice are our routine friction. Project Bookmark, their statistical promoter-finder, is a secondary tool.

name: ECUST
title: The Great Wall
relevance: direct competitor on optogenetics; technique to borrow on light-delivery hardware. Treat the modelled "42.7% greater antigen transport" as a simulation output, not a measurement — the abstract says the model predicted it.
why: Light-programmable bacteria using LOV–CheZ fusions for protein-level control of motility — regulation at the protein rather than the transcriptional level, which is a different lever from CcaSR. Three variants built, best candidate gave larger swimming halos under blue light than in darkness, and they wrote bacterial tracking software plus an agent-based model. They also built an illuminated screw immersion device, so there is real illumination hardware to inspect.

name: Guelph
title: Lumifert
relevance: competitor on optogenetics; new direction on the commercialisation / continued-R&D bucket the advisor's brief asks about.
why: A duckweed-plus-*Gluconacetobacter* consortium accumulating N and P under optogenetic regulation, produced on-site at the farm, with an explicit commercialisation argument and ongoing industry consultation. Optogenetic control of a nutrient pathway in a two-organism system is a harder control problem than ReLeaf's single chassis.

name: HiZJU-China
title: UNICO-fuel
relevance: same space
why: `same space` on the mechanism that matters most to us — a light-controlled CRISPRi system used to dynamically balance cell growth against product synthesis in engineered P. pastoris, with auxotrophic containment, suicide switches and radiation protection on top. Growth-versus-production is the trade-off our green-light schedule BO is optimising, and they attack it with light and repression rather than scheduling. The upstream photocatalytic CO2-to-methanol step is chemistry, not biology, and the abstract gives no titre for epi-isozizaene.

name: Hongwen School
title: BrewXOS
relevance: technique to borrow — multi-enzyme co-secretion from *B. subtilis* with a quantified yield, which is what ReLeaf cannot yet report.
why: *B. subtilis* engineered with three complementary enzymes so that enzyme production and substrate conversion happen in one fermentation with no purified enzyme added — a secretion result with an actual number attached (control-adjusted 107.9 mg xylose equivalents per gram dry substrate at 12 h). They also built a compact fermentation-monitoring prototype.

name: ICJFLS
title: ORA-GUARD: Engineered Oral Probiotics for Long-Term Bad Breath Solution
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — genome integration plus secretion in a Gram-positive commensal is the nearest analogue to what we need in *B. subtilis*.
why: Three of our weak spots in one booth: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated genome integration (not a plasmid) into *Streptococcus salivarius* K12, a codon-optimised multi-enzyme system secreting volatile-sulfur-degrading enzymes, and layered containment combining auxotrophy with a temperature-sensitive kill switch. "Efficiently secretes" and "precise and sustained" are claims with no numbers attached — worth pressing.

name: KULeuven
title: EMPOWER: Engineering Microbes to Promote Ovarian Wellbeing and Recovery
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — a parts-characterisation protocol for an awkward chassis, and a reason to re-express our CcaSR characterisation in more than one reporter.
why: Before the therapy, they built the missing toolkit for a non-model anaerobe, *Phocaeicola vulgatus*: characterised promoters evaluated across four fluorescent reporters, optimised conjugation, and phenotypic characterisation of candidate chassis strains. Using four reporters rather than one is a measurement choice almost nobody else in this slice made.

name: NUS-SPS
title: AEGIS: Astro-Engineered Guardian of Interface Surfaces
relevance: same space
why: `same space` and the closest architectural neighbour in the slice — a non-pathogenic B. subtilis strain with an optogenetic switch wired to biofilm-thinning genes, so external light controls biofilm on demand, used to competitively exclude biofilm-forming E. coli in the ISS water processor. Light in, B. subtilis phenotype out, in a flow system: that is ReLeaf's control loop pointed at a different output. Ecological competition as the mitigation strategy is a genuinely different idea from killing the incumbent.

name: RUM-UPRM
title: R-DetoX 2.5
relevance: competitor on the bioreactor; benchmark for how to report a reactor result. Note they label SeBiS 2.0 as proposed, not built.
why: A real reactor claim with a real measurement behind it — 85% extracellular substrate reduction in 20 hours by HPLC with abiotic controls unchanged — plus SeBiS 2.0, a proposed serial bioreactor integrating growth, continuous treatment, biomass recirculation and byproduct mitigation. Biomass recirculation in a serial train is a configuration ReLeaf's closed loop has not addressed.

name: Stony Brook
title: Engineering Bacteria to Detect and Break Down Biofilms Secreted by *S. aureus*
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — a YebF secretion failure case with a named culprit is worth more to us than three successes.
why: Three enzymes pushed out through a YebF carrier, and they report exactly which ones worked: secretion confirmed for Nuclease1 and SspA, eDNA degradation confirmed, SspA proteolytically active — and Dispersin B stayed membrane-embedded and untested. They also state that biofilm degradation itself remains undemonstrated. Two-signal detection (AI-2 early, nitric oxide late) with an arabinose-inducible mazE/mazF kill switch.

name: SYPHU-China
title: LBP-Mototype: An Environment-Dependent Suicide Strategy for IBD Live Biotherapeutics
relevance: ** New direction — our kill switch should probably be environment-dependent rather than toxin-based, since outside the bioreactor there is no bile but there are other absent nutrients.
why: The only containment design here that does not introduce a toxin. Deleting acrB and pspA weakens bile efflux and membrane protection; inflammation-responsive PspA complementation conditionally restores protection while AcrB stays absent, so ambient bile stress is the killing agent and the genetic killing chain gets shorter. They also think about the awkward parts — protein carry-over buffering the signal, par⁻-associated inheritance variation producing graded survival.

name: Texas
title: Engineering Probiotics to Combat Malnutrition
relevance: none-but-instructive, sharply so — this is the failure mode ReLeaf is most likely to hit.
why: They fused an enzyme to YebF expecting secretion and got membrane localisation instead — then confirmed the localisation and showed the activity anyway. A documented, diagnosed secretion failure with the assays that caught it is worth more to GEMS than a dozen successful constructs. They also ran MICOM community metabolic modelling and report a negative finding from it.

name: Tongji China
title: Virock: Intelligent Microbial Self-Healing Concrete System
relevance: same space
why: `same space` — B. subtilis as chassis, expressing mineralisation-assisting proteins for calcium carbonate deposition in concrete cracks, with a biosafety containment system that restricts survival outside the intended environment via cell lysis and growth inhibition. Same chassis, same problem of a deliberately released engineered organism, different application. The abstract is written almost entirely in intent ("designs", "we expect") with no deposition rates or crack-closure data.

name: TUS-Japan
title: Soilmate
relevance: direct competitor — and the single most useful technique-to-borrow booth in the slice.
why: This is ReLeaf's enzyme on ReLeaf's chassis for ReLeaf's problem — ACC deaminase on engineered *Bacillus subtilis* to relieve salt-induced ethylene stress. Their route is different and arguably smarter: rather than secreting into the medium they display the enzyme on the surface using a Twin-arginine translocation signal plus a LysM domain anchor, and they explicitly frame it as avoiding modification of the crop. The Tat pathway choice is a direct answer to the question GEMS has not solved.

name: Virginia
title: ChronoContain
relevance: technique to borrow
why: they argue that environment-triggered biocontainment fails precisely when real-world conditions change, and replace the trigger with a clock: a modular timed kill switch in E. coli using phage holin–antiholin systems to lyse the cells after a defined interval. For an organism we intend to release to plants through a membrane, a timer is a far more defensible containment story than a chemical or nutrient trigger. No escape frequency or timing spread is reported.

name: Waterloo
title: Biofilm Busters: Targeting Pathogenic Gut Biofilms Through Curli Inhibition
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — comparing their YebF experience against Stony Brook's gives two data points on the same carrier, and the off-target taxa survey is a model for asking which soil organisms our protectants touch.
why: The second independent YebF secretion case in this slice — an N-terminal YebF carrier to secrete CsgC, a natural amyloid chaperone, so the mechanism inhibits curli assembly rather than killing bacteria. They plan a move to *Lactococcus lactis* with inducible expression and biological containment, and used bioinformatics to survey curli genes across gut taxa to predict which organisms would be hit.

name: XMU-China
title: STING: Small TnpB-based Innovative Nuclease toolkit
relevance: technique to borrow
why: the one containment claim in the slice with a number attached — a self-targeting biocontainment circuit reducing bacterial survival by up to five orders of magnitude. The rest is a compact TnpB editing toolkit with per-host efficiency ranges honestly spread (4.2–100% deletion in E. coli, 30–44% in P. putida), structure-guided evolution to five noncanonical TAMs, and registered core parts. Reporting a range that starts at 4.2% rather than a best case is unusual here.

name: Aachen
title: Adesonica
relevance: ** Technique to borrow, and the closest benchmark in the slice for our own reactor-plus-software stack.
why: They built M.A.R.M.A.L.A.D.E., a two-compartment automated reactor — bacteria express TMV coat protein in the first part, virus-like particles assemble in the second — plus the control software for it. Separately they trained an ML model to predict the transcriptome from the methylome specifically to cut measurement cost, and packaged growth-rate prediction from transcriptomics as a Python library.

name: EPFL
title: OrbitAl
relevance: technique to borrow
why: two things we need. First a designed protein that folds around Al3+, an ion with no natural biological sensor, plus engineered E. coli reporters that distinguish Fe(III) from Fe(II) — speciation, not just concentration. Second, and more important for us, mass spectrometry quantifies the same samples so the biological signal always has a chemical reference. They also built a balloon-borne sampler that keeps stratospheric aerosols intact and uncontaminated to the lab.

name: GeorgetownPrep
title: SENTINEL-LOOP
relevance: technique to borrow — the provenance convention and the orthogonal-verification habit.
why: They verify their own biosensors with an orthogonal method — bismuth-film screen-printed electrodes and square-wave anodic stripping voltammetry — and their open-source analysis pipeline carries provenance labels that separate simulated from experimental evidence. They also state plainly that wet-lab validation was incomplete at Wiki Freeze. That combination of independent verification plus provenance labelling is the measurement-rigour practice GEMS should copy outright.

name: Houston-TX
title: AKGut: Model-Guided Design of a Probiotic that Produces α-Ketoglutarate
relevance: ** Benchmark — this is the standard our digital twin should be judged against, i.e. modelling that produces decisions and catches errors rather than a figure.
why: This is the only team in the slice where modelling demonstrably changed the build: flux balance analysis on iHM1533 named glutamate dehydrogenase (not α-KG dehydrogenase) as the main drain, put the production optimum near half-maximal oxygen, showed no knockout set couples production to growth, and caught a residue-numbering error that would have put the citrate synthase mutation one residue off. They also say the chromosomal knockouts are still in troubleshooting.

name: Jilin-China
title: NutriTrace
relevance: new direction — the strongest idea in the slice for the digital twin and the AI sensor layer.
why: A living DNA recorder in *Komagataella phaffii*: stress-responsive promoters driving site-specific recombinases so each cell permanently writes its own stress history, read out by fluorescence after the run, with cells in alginate beads for recovery. Their stated motive is exactly ReLeaf's blind spot — that tank-average probes hide local gradients of nutrients, oxygen and metabolites. This is a way to validate a digital twin against what cells actually experienced, not what the probe at one port saw.

name: Mingdao
title: Ethanol from Paper Waste
relevance: same space
why: `same space` as a vessel-building team, and Taiwanese, so worth the contact regardless. They built a benchtop fermentor, ran one-pot simultaneous saccharification and fermentation with cellulase, β-glucosidase and Zymomonas mobilis on plastic-lined paper containers, and — the part worth copying — characterised both enzymes under fermentation-compatible conditions far from their optima, then modelled the enzyme–microbe coupling. Characterising a component at the condition you will actually run it at, not at its optimum, is precisely the discipline our CcaSR induction work needed. No ethanol yield is given.

name: NTHU Taiwan
title: CatharSys
relevance: direct competitor and benchmark for the bioreactor build.
why: Engineered industrial *B. subtilis* in a moving bed biofilm reactor, and they built CathaBench, a three-tank laboratory reactor with automated sensing and control, plus three layers of biosafety measures. This is the closest hardware analogue to ReLeaf in the slice: same chassis, same reactor-plus-instrumentation posture, and a Taiwanese team at a semiconductor-wastewater problem.

name: NUS-Singapore
title: ORCHID: Observation of Real-time Cellular Health and Intracellular Dynamics for Predictive Biomanufacturing
relevance: benchmark
why: they build modular multiplexed intracellular biosensors that report several stress signals at once during a culture, and feed that high-dimensional stream into ML to predict titre/rate/yield before the process degrades. Their stated argument is exactly ours — current practice is reactive, adjusting conditions after the damage shows — but their sensor lives inside the cell rather than in the vessel wall. The abstract claims predictive insight without naming a single prediction horizon, accuracy figure or test fermentation, so the claim is at the same maturity as our own anomaly layer.

name: Patras-Med
title: ICHNOS: Trace the Invisible
relevance: technique to borrow
why: a stress-responsive sensor drives a TetR circuit and a tandem fluorescent timer, so the cell records the intensity and timing of a stress event that has since faded; ICHNOS-Vail then estimates the past event from image analysis plus a model. That is our two-event finding in the 434 h run solved biologically instead of statistically — a record written by the cells rather than inferred from a photodiode trace.

name: PuiChing-Macau
title: Tuning butyrate with engineered probiotics to prevent Alzheimer's
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — negative feedback inside the cell is the alternative to doing all regulation in our external controller.
why: The circuit is a closed loop with an explicit brake: a pNorVβ promoter senses nitric oxide, and butyrate biosynthesis runs under a negative feedback loop specifically to prevent overproduction. They also claim customised delivery hardware, risk-prediction software and a personalised dosage model — an unusual high-school combination, and the hardware/software claims are thin enough in the abstract to be worth probing.

name: Saarland
title: OWLET
relevance: technique to borrow — calibration methodology, almost directly transferable to the OD600 channel.
why: A low-cost 3D-printed fluorescence reader that pumps water into a six-well strip, measures fluorescence and converts it into fluorescein-equivalent units, validated against fluorescein standards and GFP-expressing E. coli — then mounted on a boat that steers toward rising signals and geotags readings. Converting raw counts into a traceable standard unit is precisely the measurement rigour GEMS wants, and it is the same problem as ReLeaf's OD600 photodiode calibration.

name: SHSID
title: PlantGuard
relevance: direct competitor on closed-loop architecture; benchmark for what the loop has to demonstrate to be believed.
why: A drought system with two modules — a chromoprotein alert in gel beads and in-situ cellulose/hyaluronic acid synthesis for rhizosphere water retention — wired to ADRS hardware with in-situ sensing, ESP32 edge computing, wireless networking and a mobile app, described as a closed sense–decide–respond loop. That is ReLeaf's control architecture applied to plant stress by a high-school team.

name: SUDA-ICPI-China
title: FLAME: An Engineered Bacterial Platform for Precision Colorectal Cancer Therapy
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — degradation tagging as a safety dial, and modelling used to choose a promoter rather than to decorate one.
why: Three-input gating — hypoxia and lactate sensing combined with LuxI/LuxR quorum sensing — with reporter data showing the strongest response under combined low oxygen and lactate, so the AND behaviour was tested, not asserted. Modelling informed promoter selection and identified limits on selectivity and achievable lesion size. They compared untagged, TAT-fused and SsrA-tagged effectors and prioritised the SsrA version on safety grounds.

name: SUSTech
title: ORCA: On-target RNA Correction of APOE4
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — the measurement-pipeline-as-deliverable pattern is directly transplantable to our OD600 and calibration work.
why: They quantify the trade-off instead of claiming a win: two candidate editors retained 61–70% target editing while cutting cumulative bystander editing in the measured APOE region by 84–88% against the parental editor. They also built SONAR plus a stated measurement pipeline to make reporter readouts reusable and interpretable, and ran protein and RNA foundation models in an explicit loop with wet-lab measurement.

name: Toronto
title: PetaBite
relevance: technique to borrow (open-source bioreactor design, PLM ranking) and benchmark for the dry-lab claim ladder.
why: They searched 27.3 million public sequencing datasets to build a 300-million-homolog enzyme database, trained a protein language model on it for candidate ranking, screen with a high-throughput copper-release assay, and test in low-cost open-source bioreactors. Both halves of Timmy's remit — a real ML pipeline and an open-hardware reactor — in one booth, with an explicit benchmark-beating goal.

name: ULethbridge
title: Utilizing MOSMAGE to engineer optimized microbial chassis
relevance: technique to borrow
why: MOSMAGE is a low-cost modular open-source hardware platform built from consumer-grade components to automate MAGE workflows, with integrated thermal, fluidics, electroporation and spectrophotometric modules. The spectrophotometric module is the same engineering problem as our in-line OD600 on low-cost photodiodes, and the fluidics-plus-thermal integration is the closest thing in the slice to an open lab-automation stack. The validation is stated in the future tense ("we will measure" TAL production), so the hardware may be further along than the biology.

name: Uni-Padua-IT
title: C.O.S.M.I.C.
relevance: technique to borrow
why: they engineered a non-invasive acoustic oxygen sensor so the vessel is never opened, and it quantifies dissolved and gaseous fractions separately — directly relevant to our in-line sensing and to the TMP/OD readings that sat below the sensor floor in the 0902 run. They also wrote ReTIsigner, an open-source codon-optimisation tool for non-standard chassis, and designed an inducible kill switch justified against planetary-protection guidelines. The chassis is Nostoc sp. PCC 7120 with pprA from D. radiodurans added for radiation tolerance.

name: UW-Poland
title: HYPPE
relevance: technique to borrow on dry-lab discipline; benchmark for how a model claim should be stated. Their pHYPPE two-reporter ratio cancels copy number and nuclear context — directly applicable to ReLeaf's MEFL-style calibration.
why: A foundation model of fungal promoters trained from scratch on a corpus they assembled — 2,702 RNA-seq runs requantified into 2,332 comparable samples across twenty genomes, every growth condition hand-annotated — encoding promoters as discrete hierarchical symbols so sequences can be read, edited and decoded back to DNA, reaching rank correlation 0.689 on a test split opened once. "Opened once" is the most disciplined ML statement in the slice.

name: William-and-Mary
title: BRO[K]EN: Building Resilient Optimized Engineered Networks
relevance: technique to borrow
why: they run longitudinal experiments on four engineered circuits in laboratory and simulated environmental conditions and try to DETECT, MITIGATE and PREDICT circuit failure from mutation, selection, burden and stress, with multitiered functional and molecular measurements. This is the failure-analysis discipline our digital twin and sentinel layer assume but have never tested — our longest record is one 434 h run.
